description: The plot illustrates how the “Sparsity Ratio of SDPA Output” (with threshold 1e-3) varies across model layers for three conditions. The x-axis is labeled “Layer,” uses a linear scale, and spans approximately layers 0 through 23 with integer tick marks at regular intervals. The y-axis is labeled “Sparsity Ratio,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from about 0.0 up to about 0.9 with evenly spaced numeric ticks (roughly 0.2 apart). Three lines are shown: a blue dashed line (no markers) labeled “sparsity ratio before gate, avg 0.003,” which stays very close to zero across all layers, starting around ~0.02 at layer 0 and remaining near ~0.00–0.01 by the final layers; an orange dotted line (no markers) labeled “sparsity ratio after gate, avg 0.126,” which starts high near ~0.85 at layer 0, drops steeply to around ~0.4 by about layer 1, continues decreasing to roughly ~0.15 by around layer 5, approaches ~0.03–0.05 by around layers 10–12, and then stays low with small fluctuations including a visible bump around layers ~19–21 (rising to roughly ~0.06–0.08) before ending near ~0.03–0.04; and a green dash-dot line (no markers) labeled “sparsity ratio after average gate, avg 0.080,” which also begins near ~0.85 at layer 0, declines sharply to about ~0.28 by around layer 1, decreases further to roughly ~0.08–0.10 by around layer 5, approaches ~0.02–0.03 by around layers 10–12, and remains near ~0.01–0.02 through the final layers.
